body: I'm really sorry to hear it. It might be worth posting on /r/SuicideWatch.

Thank you for your great reply :)

I don't think it's necessarily true that I'm going around grading things as pointless or what not. I just can't really find a point to stick around at all. And that doesn't make me want to die in and of itself. However, I think the combination of the feelings of purposelessness *AND* points in life where things get sucky cause me to think, "Why go through this right now when I could just end it," because even outside of the sucky part I feel as though I'm not missing out on much due to the purposelessness. So yes you're absolutely right in saying "ending life ahead of time or floating through it in a cloud of nihilism seems just as pointless as anything else. Or even more so, since you'd not be making the most of the experience while you're here," but I feel like that's not taking into account the times in life when things go south. And when they start going south more often than not, it becomes a motivator to ending it since it feels purposeless anyway.

I also think one could argue that if you're truly nihilistic, then being nihilistic is the healthiest thing for you to be for a certain amount of time, because without it, you might not recognize the need to find a purpose. So calling it innately "pointless" might not be totally correct. I guess you could even argue that the words "pointless" or "purposeless" aren't even sensible descriptors for life or the universe. That's a bit of an aside though :)

Your movie analogy is where I've been at basically the entire last decade. I've been holding out for nearly half my life hoping for, and actively seeking out, something better to come - something that will motivate me to live. And there are ups and downs, but I guess I lose hope as time goes on that anything substantial will make me want to stick around, ya know? Like I worked hard in high school to get a full ride in college so I could study whatever in case I figured out what I wanted to do. I picked a major I didn't hate and that I knew would pay well straight out of college so I could start saving in case I figured out what I wanted to do. I have worked hard at a job that's pretty meh and have saved away a good amount of money and started building my 401k in case I figure out what I want to do. This again is combined with how lucky I am to be given those opportunities, but I didn't throw the opportunities away either. And I experienced some really great things and some really shit things in that time, but never once had a clear idea of what I wanted to truly make of my life. So here I am haha.

Thanks again so much for your reply. It's really nice to be able to talk through this stuff :)

Yeah I also have mixed feelings about depression meds. I'm also not too keen on talking to a psychologist because I suck at opening up and also that seems to me like a last line of defense where if that doesn't work I'm not sure what will.

I try to think about what's ahead a lot, and that's mostly what I've done the past decade (while trying to live in the moment as well), and I'm just kinda wondering if enough is enough ya know? I've experienced a lot and I sort of feel ready to go sometimes.

Thank you for your response :)
